item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00157","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C09","C03","C14"],"selected_candidate_label":"C09","confidence":0.93,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C09 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child's treatment of international agreements and foreign-policy supervision. Its paired provisions assign negotiation and entry into agreements to the Secretary of State and make functions under the governing Act subject to the Secretary's foreign-policy responsibilities; the child reproduces this same two-part machinery in section 4 with closely parallel language. C03 contains an especially similar compact pair of clauses and is a strong alternative, but C09 more closely matches the child's formulation in terms of functions under an Act and the sequence of agreement authority followed by foreign-policy responsibility. C14 contains the same machinery in a broader and less compact administrative order.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The functions of negotiating and entering into international agreements under the Act shall be performed by or under the authority of the Secretary of State.","parent_excerpt":"The functions of negotiating and entering into agreements with friendly nations or organizations of friendly nations conferred upon the President by the Act are hereby delegated to the Secretary of State.","explanation":"Both use the same distinctive formulation to place negotiation and execution of agreements under the Secretary of State."},{"child_excerpt":"International cooperation under the Act shall be subject to the responsibilities of the Secretary of State with respect to the foreign policy of the United States pertinent thereto.","parent_excerpt":"All functions under the Act, however vested, delegated, or assigned, shall be subject to the responsibilities of the Secretary of State with respect to the foreign policy of the United States as such policy relates to the said functions.","explanation":"The child closely adapts C09's foreign-policy supervision clause to atomic-energy cooperation."},{"child_excerpt":"SEC. 4. (a) ... negotiating and entering into international agreements ... Secretary of State. (b) International cooperation under the Act shall be subject to the responsibilities of the Secretary of State...","parent_excerpt":"SEC. 3. Department of State. (a) The functions of negotiating and entering into agreements ... are hereby delegated to the Secretary of State. (b) All functions under the Act ... shall be subject to the responsibilities of the Secretary of State...","explanation":"The same paired operative sequence—agreement authority followed immediately by a State Department foreign-policy proviso—is material structural evidence of reuse."}]}
